title: The closed counit on abelian pro-etale sheaves
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention], the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let i:Z→X be an arbitrary closed immersion of schemes. On sheaves of abelian groups, the actual inverse-image/direct-image adjunction counit i*i_*→id is an isomorphism. Equivalently i_* is fully faithful. There is no quasi-compact-open-complement, qcqs-base, reducedness, or finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09BL and 09BK: closed immersions, affine closed-site lift and counit.

proof.text: For a quotient immersion Spec(A/I) → Spec A, the closed-site adjunction v ⊣ b has invertible unit. Its opposite, whiskered into abelian-group-valued presheaves, has invertible counit. Thus precomposition with b.op is fully faithful. Cocontinuity of v gives continuity of b, so this precomposition restricts to sheaves. The fully faithful sheaf-to-presheaf inclusions show that the resulting pushforward on affine-basis sheaves is fully faithful.

Restriction to the affine ind-etale bases is an equivalence on sheaves, and the square comparing these restrictions with the actual direct image commutes by the base-change formula. Cancel the faithful restriction functor to deduce full faithfulness of actual direct image for the quotient immersion. Any closed immersion into an affine scheme is isomorphic to a quotient immersion, so composition and isomorphism invariance give the affine case. The counit of its actual adjunction is invertible by full faithfulness of the right adjoint.

For a square with weakly etale horizontal arrows, form the restriction base-change map from Over.pullbackMapComparison. It is invertible when the square is cartesian. Its mate under the horizontal restriction/direct-image adjunctions is the canonical isomorphism comparing the two composites of direct images. This identity is checked on presheaf sections, using the unit and counit of the site map/pullback adjunction and the universal property of pullbacks. The double-mate identity therefore makes the corresponding inverse-image comparison invertible. The mate-counit identity expresses the restriction of the actual global counit as a composite of isomorphisms whenever the local vertical counit is invertible.

Pull back an affine open cover of X along i. Each local vertical closed immersion has affine target, so its counit is invertible by the affine case. The preceding cartesian-square calculation makes every open restriction of the global counit invertible. Apply the existing theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction from WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.LowerShriek.OpenImmersion.Conservative. It is stated directly for continuous pushforward along the localization site functor, so is independent of either pullback API. These open restrictions are jointly conservative: on each weakly etale object use the covering sieve generated by the base changes of the open cover, and apply the sheaf-local criterion for an isomorphism. Hence every component of the global counit, and then the counit itself, is invertible. No quasi-compact complement, reducedness, or finite-presentation assumption is used; the empty closed scheme is included.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09AA, 09BL and 09BK. B3: full faithfulness via the opposite closed-site adjunction and affine restriction equivalences; global counit via restriction base change, double mates and open-cover conservativity. The categorical restriction calculation follows the proved library WeaklyEtale and OpenImmersion.Conservative modules, with the existing conservativity theorem reused through its API-independent restriction functor statement; the base-change calculation is specialized to the finite-coefficient API.
